title: Wrap tutorEditProfile's read-then-overwrite in a transaction to stop the lost-update race
why: Every other stateful mutation needing read-then-write consistency in this file (acceptTutorInvite, revokeTutorGrant, resignTutorGrant, expirePendingInvites) wraps it in db.runTransaction. tutorEditProfile instead reads the profile doc, merges edit fields in application memory, then does a full-document `set(..., {merge:false})` with no transaction. If the owner's own device (or a second tutor) writes any other field to the same learner_profiles/{profileId} doc between the get() and the set(), that write is silently overwritten by tutorEditProfile's stale full-doc replace -- a lost-update race, undermining the very H2 fix comment that motivated reading the full doc first.
recommendation: Wrap the read+write in db.runTransaction (txn.get + txn.set), consistent with the rest of the file, or switch to `profilePath.set(updates, {merge:true})` for the scalar fields being edited -- Firestore applies a merge write atomically server-side without a client-side read first.
acceptance_criteria: A concurrency test (a second writer updates an unrelated profile field between tutorEditProfile's get and set) shows that field survives.
